 By T. RAHULESH 
 Wednesday, 28 Oct 2026

 Heart-to-heart talk: Tee Kai Wun (right) hopes his partner Man Wei Chong will gain more confidence in upcoming tournaments. 
 PETALING JAYA: Sometimes all that is needed to jolt you into action is a candid conversation with a friend.
 Following a disappointing first round exit at the Denmark Open two weeks ago, national doubles shuttler Tee Kai Wun felt the need to address his partner, Man Wei Chong, directly.
 “After Denmark, I had a discussion with Wei Chong,” said Kai Wun upon arriving at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) yesterday.
 “I told him that if he wants to win, he has to change his own mindset first. Only then can I help him.”
 The pair had spent several months apart earlier this year, with Kai Wun combining with other players while Wei Chong recovered from a right knee injury sustained in March.
 During this period, Kai Wun claimed the Korean Masters title alongside Yap Roy King in August.
 Wei Chong, however, struggled to find his form. The lack of titles – his last came when he won the 2025 Malaysian Masters with Kai Wun – began to heavily affect the 27-year-old’s confidence.
 But Kai Wun’s words left a lasting impact on Wei Chong and quickly bore fruit as the world No. 8 pair captured their first Super 750 title at the French Open on Sunday.
 “We didn’t really expect this because we didn’t play well in Denmark,” Kai Wun admitted.
 “I think after this tournament, Wei Chong will regain his confidence.”
 Kai Wun, 26, noted that while the victory is a significant boost, his partner still needs to manage his ongoing injury.
 “We still have three tournaments left to end the year.
 “We’ll just try to play our best.”
 The duo will next compete at the Korean Open from Nov 3-8.
